question: What was the actual growth rate of the first five-year plan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in 1951 and lasted until 1956.
 
• The primary objective of the First Five-Year Plan was to improve the living standards of the people of India by making judicious use of the country's resources.
 
• The plan focused heavily on agriculture, irrigation, and energy to boost the economy.
 
• The actual growth rate achieved during the First Five-Year Plan was 3.6% (0.036), which was more than the targeted growth rate of 2.1% (0.021).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans**

 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were a series of centralized economic and social growth initiatives in India, modeled after the Soviet Union's own plans.
 
• They aimed to create a balance in the country's economy and promote steady growth in various sectors such as agriculture, industry, and services.
 
• The Planning Commission, an institution in the Government of India, was responsible for drafting and executing these plans.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan focused mainly on the agricultural sector to address the food shortage that the country was facing post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• It was established in March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India.
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) in 2015.
 
• The commission played a crucial role in allocating resources, formulating policies, and defining the direction of economic development in the country.
 
 
 
• **Economic Growth Rate**
 
 
• The economic growth rate is a measure of the increase in a country’s economic output and is often calculated as the percentage increase in the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• It is an important indicator of economic health and is used by policymakers to gauge the effectiveness of economic policies.
 
• A higher growth rate indicates a thriving economy with more jobs and higher income levels, while a lower rate may suggest economic problems.
